clue.text: What could be my one way to make payment?

definitions.meaning: the letters of 'my one' put in a new order make a familiar word for cash, so the phrase describes itself as an order of that word
the straight reading: a postal instrument for sending a sum to someone

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud which method to use to settle a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Reordering MY ONE gives MONEY, so the answer is literally a MONEY ORDER; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A money order is a prepaid paper instrument bought at a post office or bank and used to send a sum safely.

clue.text: You'll find him among German novelists

definitions.text: You'll find him among German novelists

indicators.note: the name sits among the letters running across the two words, straddling their join

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the end of German and the start of novelists

explanation.surface: A pointer to where a particular writer is shelved or listed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle gerMAN Novelists, and Thomas Mann is himself one of the great German novelists, so the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann, author of Buddenbrooks and The Magic Mountain, is a celebrated twentieth-century German writer of fiction.

clue.text: Very much in the minority

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British colloquial emphatic agreement
second meaning: literally less than a half, so making up fewer than fifty per cent

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses pull opposite ways: the slang phrase means 'enormously', while read literally it means a small share.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the phrase as an emphatic 'yes, extremely', while literally a portion that is not half is a lesser share.

clue.text: At sea, with this, many chaps could be sailing craft

indicators.note: confused or all over the place, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: With good seamanship, a crowd of men could manage the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sits naturally in a nautical surface, hiding its role as the jumbling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft here means skill, so sailing craft is the art of handling a yacht well.

clue.text: Where people engage in recreation or in relaxation

indicators.note: the short word is placed within the word for relaxation

parts.note: rest is a period of relaxation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a holiday place where people play or unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers two alternative descriptions of a holiday spot; only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination visited for leisure, such as a seaside town or ski centre.

clue.text: Spells out different way to make axle spin

indicators.note: arranging the letters a different way forms a new word, so the phrase is the jumbling signal

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Instructions describe an alternative method of getting an axle to rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell something out is to make it plain in detail, which is what one does when one clarifies it.

clue.text: Slowly move part of foot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to edge forward bit by bit
second meaning: a twelfth of the imperial unit of length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' suggests the body part, but it is the unit of length that contains twelve of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for creeping forward gradually and an imperial measure equal to one twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Lack of care showing, ultimately, in name chosen

indicators.note: the final letter is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: the elect are those chosen, as in a president-elect

indicators.note: at the very end, so only the last letter of the word showing is used

parts.note: the word showing ends in G, its last letter

explanation.surface: Negligence is apparent in the name that was selected.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is the failure to give proper attention or care to something or someone.

clue.text: Gold, for example, found in this kind of rock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gold is a dense element
second meaning: a loud guitar-driven style of rock music

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gold ore in a geological rock; the second sense is rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists class dense elements like gold and lead as heavy metals, and the phrase also names a loud, distorted genre of music.

clue.text: Reviews revised section once it's edited

editing alters it, reinforcing that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to reorder

explanation.definitionFit: Notices are critics' written assessments of a play, book or performance in a newspaper.

clue.text: American serving in country area or city in Italy

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
a GI is an enlisted soldier in the US army

explanation.definitionFit: Perugia is the capital of Umbria in central Italy, a hilltop city known for its university and chocolate.

clue.text: Controls people around gallery with little time for restoration

men as a general word for people

clue.text: Change in indigenous fashion, otherwise

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.definitionFit: Alternatively and otherwise both introduce another possibility or option.

clue.text: Irish writer first covering English game in Africa

parts.note: best as in top or first-placed

explanation.surface: An Irish author is first to cover an English sport in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sport, but it means wild animals hunted or watched.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large antelope of the African savanna, and game means wild animals.

indicators.note: leaving out the letters for one and Liberal from the preceding phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, being famous for something wicked or shameful.

clue.text: Strange taste in European liqueur

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Like fairytale emperor or king, surrounded by curious people

parts.note: starers are people gawping out of curiosity

clue.text: Split in duties after reorganisation

indicators.note: once the letters have been reorganised they form the answer

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to reorganise

clue.text: A clot is strangely able to endure suffering

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A foolish person is, oddly, able to bear pain.

clue.text: This hat, passed round, gets a chap a little money

parts.note: taken as written, the article before chap
a man is a chap
taken as written, the article before little money
p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight brimmed straw hat, originally woven in Ecuador.

clue.text: Top marks, bad mark? Stay neutral, in a way

parts.note: A and B are the two highest grades

kin are relatives

clue.text: Create borders, those of England and Greece

clue.text: Head in certain direction as prisoner on the loose

clue.text: Northern country in which I caught antelope

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the eland is a large African antelope

clue.text: Part of hospital lunch that's hard to swallow
